Build it on a coarse grid of about 144x174 art pixels and blow every art pixel up into a solid square of ONE flat colour about 5-6 canvas pixels wide, all squares the same size, all aligned to one single grid. There must be no in-between colour anywhere in the image: no anti-aliased edge pixels, no soft colour ramps, no airbrushed cheeks, no gradient fills, no glossy specular blobs, no blur, no strand-by-strand hair, no thin tapering lines, no line thinner than one block, no speckled noise, no scattered stray single pixels. An ordered checkerboard of two tones is the ONLY permitted blend. The whole image uses at most about 28 colours. This is emphatically NOT anime, NOT manga, NOT vector lineart, NOT a semi-realistic digital painting — it is the deliberate, blocky, hand-placed pixel work of the reference image.
LIGHT — restrained, one warm overhead key. The ENTIRE figure — hair, hat, both shoulders, both upper arms and anything held — sits inside the canvas with clear empty space above the head and at least 8% of the canvas width of empty background beyond the widest point on the left and on the right. The figure must meet the background with a HARD one-block edge; no soft, feathered or semi-transparent halo of any kind may surround the silhouette, because the pipeline keys that colour out and any haze survives as a dirty fringe.
No text, no lettering, no watermark, no signature, no border, no frame, no UI chrome, no brand marks or logos on any garment or object.
PALETTE BUDGET (hard, and the axis every round has failed on): the finished image must contain AT MOST 28 distinct colours in total, and every single one of them must cover a large connected area — no colour may exist as a handful of scattered pixels or as a one-block transition between two other colours.
